This is a legitimate test-isolation technique with no demonstrated exposure.

observations.title: Behavioral test suite compiles functions from the project's own source
observations.technical_explanation: All five flagged calls belong to a single test that isolates extension functions by textually slicing the project's main source between fixed function-name markers and compiling the slices with the Function constructor, passing only literals and stubs. The containing file is a standalone Node test runner that reads its own repository files and executes assertion-based tests, and it is not referenced by the extension manifest, which loads a single browser script. This code therefore does not execute in the SillyTavern client and does not process external data. The dynamic-execution matches reflect a test-bootstrap technique rather than an exploitable or malicious code path.
observations.layman_explanation: The flagged lines are all part of the project's own developer test file. It copies pieces of the extension's code into a sandbox to check behavior with fixed example values. Nothing about this uses your data, keys, or connections.

observations.title: Widget geometry tests compile functions from the project's own source
observations.technical_explanation: The flagged call is part of a test that extracts geometry helper functions from the project's main source and compiles them with the Function constructor using numeric literals, a mocked viewport, and a stub document. The file is a standalone Node test runner, not the extension's declared browser entry point, and the generated code is fed only fixed test values. No attacker-influenced data, credentials, or runtime host state reaches the constructor, and there is no network, storage, or persistence behavior in the flagged code. The match is consistent with legitimate test isolation rather than a security-relevant dynamic-execution risk.
